title: The gated layer in a cell model
observableEvidence: Uses a provided cell model to select the main role an identified part plays for the whole cell, without biochemical detail.
prompt:
A class finished a model of a plant cell and wrote this description of its two outer layers.

Cell wall: the outermost layer. It is thick and stiff, and it keeps the same shape when the model is pressed.

Cell membrane: a thin, bendable layer just inside the cell wall. It has small gates. In the model, water and food materials pass through the gates into the cell, and waste passes out through them. Some other materials are kept out at the gates.

Based on this model, what is the main job of the cell membrane for the whole cell?
solutionRepresentation: The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell. The model shows its gates letting some materials in and waste out while keeping other materials out, so it sorts what passes rather than letting everything through or blocking everything. Stiff support belongs to the cell wall, which is the thick, stiff outer layer in the model.
solutionMethod: Match each described feature of the cell membrane in the model (thin, bendable, with gates that let some materials pass and keep others out) to a job for the whole cell, and rule out the job that belongs to the cell wall.

hintSteps.prompt: Look closely at how the model describes the cell membrane, especially its gates.
hintSteps.question: What happens to different materials when they reach the gates?

hintSteps.prompt: Make a two-row table, one row for each outer layer. Write each layer's features: one is thick and stiff; the other is thin, bendable and has gates. Then write a job that fits each set of features.
hintSteps.question: Which job in the answer list fits every feature you wrote for the thin layer, and which job fits the thick layer instead?

hintSteps.prompt: A different example: a school has strong outer walls and a front office. The walls hold the building up. The front office checks people, letting some come in or go out and turning others away. The walls support; the office sorts.
hintSteps.question: Which layer of the model cell works like the front office, and what does that tell you about its job?
